text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Electricity group Endesa clashes with Industry Minister Josep Pique over new structure of electricity sector.
- Spain's opposition Socialist party accuses government of breaking all its promises with 1997 budget.
- Bishops condemn luxury of Deputy Prime Minister Francisco Alvarez Cascos' wedding last Saturday.
EL MUNDO
- Socialist MP Jose Borrell accuses ruling conservative party of increasing inequality in 1997 budget.
DIARIO 16
- Church warns Cascos that his second marriage is void according because he is divorced.
ABC
- Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato assures that 1997 budget will guarantee solidarity and employment while Borrell attacks budget on behalf of Socialist leader Felipe Gonzalez.
CINCO DIAS
- Bank stocks boost Madrid stock market as they reach year highs and attract funds flowing from electricity sector.
- Rato focuses on fall in consumer prices as success of government's economic policy, toning down importance of salary freeze.
EXPANSION
- Spain's stock market watchdog, CNMV, investigates trading in electricity companies Sevillana and Fecsa.
- Rato presents measures to opposition parties that will guarantee entry into European economic and monetary union.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Government eliminates tax deduction for capital investment.
- Catalan leader Jordi Pujol says government should confront structural reforms with courage and not with fear of losing votes.
- Reorganisation of electricity sector will not only affect electricity companies; banks will have to revise their investments in these companies.
